reason: I want to expose ice below the windblown surface; the shovel seems suited to removing loose cover.
expectation: I expect to uncover a cleaner part of the bank, though I may need another tool to sample it.

alternatives.reason: The hammer might extract ice directly, but I would clear the surface first.

effect: The shovel produced ice-rich rubble, so the exposed material can now be worked with the hammer.
reaction: That fits the goal, though I expected a cleared bank rather than rubble.
reason: I want to break the rubble into a usable sample and the hammer is a natural tool for it.
expectation: I expect smaller pieces or an ice sample suitable for examination.

alternatives.reason: The dry bank sample is also relevant, but I want to finish collecting ice first.

effect: The rubble is now a trimmed block, ready to put in a sample jar.
reaction: That makes physical sense and feels like progress toward examining the ice.
reason: A jar should contain the ice sample for examination.
expectation: I expect to collect a jarred ice sample, perhaps revealing how to inspect it.

effect: The ice is sealed as chips and can be inspected with the lens.
reaction: The change from block to chips was a small surprise but fits collecting a sample.
reason: The lens is the obvious way to examine the collected ice.
expectation: I expect a visible description of the ice and perhaps a clue about its history.

alternatives.reason: I also want the dry material, but the ice is ready to inspect now.

effect: The brown line suggests a deposit predating the upper ice, and the next goal is the dry bank.
reaction: I like that a small visible detail gives a reason to wonder about the site's history.
reason: Collecting dry bank material is the only gameplay option and directly serves the new goal.
expectation: I expect a jarred sample of loose dry material to examine.

effect: The dry material is collected and ready for the lens.
reaction: As expected; nothing especially notable yet.
reason: The lens is the only gameplay option and should reveal the sample's features.
expectation: I expect a description of the grains and possibly a comparison with the ice band.

effect: The dry sample has distinct pale chips and dark angular grains, while the ice contains finer buried brown material; both samples are retained and the ice must stay frozen.
reaction: The contrast is intriguing, although I would like a clearer sense of what the different grains might imply.

mostWorthwhile.text: Examining the ice revealed a brown line beneath later ice, turning a simple sample into a clue about the bank's past.

leastWorthwhile.text: Collecting and trimming the rubble felt like straightforward preparation with little feedback beyond the item names.

surprise.text: The brown line was buried within the ice, suggesting an earlier deposit rather than just surface dust.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless; the shovel, hammer, jars and lens all had plausible uses, though the block becoming chips was implicit.

continue.text: Yes, I would continue to see what analysis makes of the samples; the layered ice raised a question I want answered, though the collection sequence was fairly linear.
